vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-gmail-reply
Version: 1.0.6

The skill bundle provides standard documentation and instructions for an AI agent to use the 'gws' CLI to reply to Gmail messages. It contains no executable code, suspicious network calls, or prompt-injection attacks, and its functionality aligns perfectly with its stated purpose in SKILL.md.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only wrapper that calls a local 'gws' CLI to reply to Gmail messages — its declared requirements align with that purpose, but the real auth/credential behavior is delegated to a separate gws-shared file that you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the instructions: the SKILL.md documents a gws gmail +reply CLI call and flags that are consistent with sending threaded replies. The only declared required binary is 'gws', which is appropriate for a CLI wrapper.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions themselves only reference invoking 'gws gmail +reply' and expected flags/files (attachments). However the SKILL.md explicitly defers auth, global flags, and security rules to ../gws-shared/SKILL.md — that external file may introduce additional behavior (credential access, auth flows, or broader CLI flags) which is not visible here and should be inspected.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files are present (instruction-only). This is low-risk from an install perspective, but it requires a pre-existing trusted 'gws' binary on PATH.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: This skill declares no environment variables or credentials itself, which is proportional. However authentication is delegated to the gws-shared SKILL.md; that file likely defines how OAuth tokens or credentials are stored/obtained. You should review gws-shared to confirm what secrets or tokens will be required and where they're stored.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request special persistence or system-wide config modification. It only invokes the local 'gws' CLI when used.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is essentially a documented wrapper around the local 'gws' CLI and looks coherent for replying to Gmail messages. Before installing or using it: (1) verify you trust the 'gws' binary on your system (confirm its origin and install method); (2) open and review ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (or run gws generate-skills only in a safe/test environment) to see how authentication and tokens are handled — that file may request OAuth tokens, credentials, or create config files; (3) be aware attachments read files you point to and the CLI will fetch original messages when composing replies; (4) if you don’t want the agent to call this skill autonomously, keep its invocation manual. If you can provide the gws-shared SKILL.md, I can re-evaluate with higher confidence.
